item.title: Spain heads into decisive election as campaigning falls silent
item.description: More than 38.6 million Spaniards are eligible to vote this Sunday in an election that could usher in a new government or keep Pedro Sánchez in power, as candidates observe a day of reflection and the Interior Ministry finalises security arrangements.

item.title: Albania: Protesters call for PM resignation amid clashs
item.description: Protesters and police have clashed on Saturday in the Albanian capital as thousands of people in anti-government protests called for Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign.

item.title: France's credit outlook cut to negative by S&P, economy minister calls it 'warning'
item.description: Rating agency S&P Global is keeping France's sovereign rating at A+ but downgrading its outlook from stable to negative. The economy minister calls this 'a very clear signal that we must have a budget'.

item.title: OpenAI and Apple accuse each other of committing trade secret theft, OpenAI countersues
item.description: OpenAI accuses Apple of stealing trade secrets through a former employee, months after Apple has launched a similar lawsuit against the ChatGPT provider.

item.title: Capsized tanker carrying 7,000 tonnes of diesel in Spain to be towed ‘immediately’ amid spill fears
item.description: The ship, carrying about 7,000 tonnes of diesel, will be towed on its side despite objections from regional officials and could reach the Spanish port of Cartagena as early as Monday.

item.title: US military denied any issues with computing platform after hack reported
item.description: Without denying having been hacked, the US military said its Cloud One computer platform was secured following media reports of US Air Force platform hack.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 28th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 28th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Australia's conservatives hope for victory in trendsetting state
item.description: Victoria's state election could deal a blow to the Prime Minister's Labor party that has been ruling the region for 12 years, in favour of the country's conservatives.

item.title: Putin unveils Russia's newest nuclear-powered submarine
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin attends a flag-raising ceremony for the nuclear-powered submarine Perm, as Russia plans to expand its submarine fleet.

item.title: US hotline to report cartel activities slammed as foreign interference by Mexico
item.description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum denounced on Friday the US hotline for reporting drug cartel activities as foreign interference.

item.title: France to create strategic rare earth reserves, with resilience coming at a cost
item.description: France aims to build reserves of critical minerals and urges Europe to invest more. Researcher Frédéric Jeannin says these stocks should protect France from market shocks and prepare its industry for a possible armed conflict.

item.title: Russia says it downed hundreds of drones as Ukraine reports first laser interception of a jet drone
item.description: Ukraine says a privately developed laser shot down a Russian jet-powered drone for the first time. Meanwhile, Russian strikes continued overnight into Saturday, damaging transport infrastructure in Dnipro and injuring five people across the Dnipropetrovsk region, regional officials say.

item.title: Ping pongonomics: Can table-tennis bring strangers together to talk about the art of play?
item.description: A new exhibition at London's Saatchi Gallery is inviting visitors to put down their phones and talk with strangers over ping pong. Created by British-French artist Charlotte Colbert, 'Conversations with Strangers' features sculptural tables designed to encourage spontaneous and sporting encounters.

item.title: How sifting through sewage could help scientists spot the next pandemic
item.description: Swiss scientists already use wastewater testing to detect flu, COVID-19 and RSV. Next, they want to use it to flag unknown threats.

item.title: What now for the EU budget after a chaotic, inconclusive summit?
item.description: A chaotic summit in Brussels has raised serious doubt over whether EU leaders will abandon their red lines and agree on a new budget by the end of the year. Here's what to expect.

item.title: US military fires at a ship that violated blockade of Iranian ports
item.description: US military maintained a "strict" blockade of Iranian ports by firing at a ship that violated the naval containment on Thursday.

item.title: Italy is turning into a solar powerhouse. But what happens when the sun goes down?
item.description: “Italy has plenty of sun, but it still runs its evenings on expensive gas – batteries can change that.”

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 28th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 28th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Where are the best places in Europe to observe the winter solstice?
item.description: The winter solstice falls on the shortest day and the longest night of the year, and across Europe this is marked with celebrations steeped in tradition.

item.title: Russia charges air force deputy chief with taking large bribe
item.description: Yuri Grekhov, 64, who oversaw procurement of aircraft, missiles and air defence systems and has been under EU sanctions since 2022, is a serving officer, unlike most of the more than a dozen senior defence figures detained since Andrei Belousov replaced Sergei Shoigu as defence minister in 2024.

item.title: Best and worst places in Europe for young people to find a job
item.description: Unemployment among 15- to 24-year-olds in the EU is three times the rate among people aged 25 to 74. Where in Europe is youth unemployment highest, and what helps explain the gap between the two age groups?

item.title: Uganda begins Africa's first mRNA Ebola vaccine trial
item.description: An experimental mRNA vaccine developed by Moderna is being tested on 224 volunteers in Uganda as health authorities seek to combat a deadly Ebola outbreak that has claimed thousands of lives in neighbouring DRC.

item.title: Europe Tonight: How do opposing Spanish parties expect to address housing or imiigration issues?
item.description: Euronews' new weekly evening show, Europe Tonight, welcomed Javier Martínez-Cantó, a Research Fellow at the Spanish National Research Center, to discuss issues such as housing and immigration, which are dominating Spain's upcoming general elections.

item.title: Estonia will close border with Russia 'to secure Europe,' foreign minister says during Baku visit
item.description: Estonia has opened its embassies in Baku and Yerevan to strengthen its strategic ties with the South Caucasus. Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna confirmed during his visit to the Azerbaijani capital that the Baltic state will close its border with Russia on 1 December.

item.title: Azerbaijani and Armenian civil societies seek 'new history' in new round of peace talks
item.description: Azerbaijan and Armenia's civil societies hold their fifth round of "Peace Bridge" talks to openly address differences and find a way forward together.

item.title: Relatives say jailed Iranian twins beaten and tortured, one faces execution
item.description: Taraneh, 21, had been held in enforced disappearance for more than three months and tortured into a confession, according to rights groups. She was sentenced to death and her twin Rumina to 25 years in prison after their arrest in Isfahan on 24 January. Both were shortlisted for the Sakharov Prize.

item.title: Serbia’s student movement puts forward Professor Saičić as its presidential candidate
item.description: Saičić was selected for his academic achievements, personal integrity and reserved public profile, which set him apart from Serbia’s established political figures.

item.title: Spain election: Will Vox be the kingmaker, and will housing decide the vote?
item.description: A prime minister candidate needs 176 votes for an absolute majority in the first vote. What are the chances of a coalition with the conservative Partido Popular?

item.title: EU enlargement back in focus: Montenegro, Moldova and Greece's 2027 role
item.description: Montenegro aims to become the EU's 28th member by 2028, while Moldova is striving to move forward on its European path despite the challenges posed by the Transnistria conflict.

item.title: Uzbek teacher turns school recycling problem into an award-winning green education project
item.description: The initiative developed in Namangan has reached 25,000 people across 25 schools. It took first place in an international competition that attracted 369 applications from 94 countries.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 27th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 27th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Italian MPs' EU committee questions the core of the hunting reform
item.description: The committee formally backed the bill, but six environmental groups say its objections should stop it in its tracks.

item.title: Europe Tonight: EU budget summit collapses as Spain braces for vote and UK unveils deal
item.description: EU budget talks collapse early in Brussels as Germany and "frugals" walk out, pushing a deal to December. Meanwhile, Spain braces for Sunday’s snap election that could unseat PM Pedro Sánchez, and Britain unveils details of its new EU cooperation deal.

item.title: German Bundestag approves record 2027 budget as borrowing hits €210bn
item.description: Record spending, substantial investment in defence and borrowing on a historic scale: the Bundestag has approved Germany’s 2027 federal budget. Meanwhile, the proposed pension reform envisages longer working lives, higher contributions and steeper penalties for early retirement.

item.title: Smolensk crash: Experts identify landing errors, rule out explosion
item.description: More than 16 years after the Smolensk disaster, prosecutors have released the findings of international experts who ruled out an explosion as the cause of the crash. Former Polish Defence Minister Antoni Macierewicz has rejected their conclusions.

item.title: Kazakh folk legends and heroes relocate to comic book pages
item.description: The Legends of the Great Steppe feature five Kazakh folk tales translated into French and Dutch for the first time.

item.title: Spain election 2026: What are voters worried about?
item.description: As the country prepares for Sunday's general election, voters in Spain have differing views on the country's political future. While some hope the left will remain in power, others support Vox and its political agenda. Housing, living costs and immigration are among the issues shaping the debate.

item.title: By Putin's logic, Russia should be returned to Mongolia, Belarus' Lukashenka says
item.description: The Belarusian leader said medieval history cannot justify territorial claims, since Russian lands were themselves once under Mongol rule, and traced East Slavic statehood to Kyivan Rus'. He then appeared to soften the remarks, saying Putin "perfectly understands this" and is "misinterpreted".

item.title: Russian drone strikes hit Ukraine's energy, rail and civilian infrastructure, causing deaths
item.description: After a series of Russian strikes and with the onset of winter cold, Ukraine was forced to halt all electricity exports, while imports reached their highest level since mid-June.

item.title: Social worker in Italy's 'family in the woods' case suspended for 70 days
item.description: The disciplinary council of Abruzzo's Order of Social Workers has sanctioned Veruska D'Angelo over her handling of the case involving the family living off-grid in Italy.

item.title: UK: London's Cake and Bake Show honours David Attenborough's centenary
item.description: From lifelike gorillas to miniature sugar sculptures of David Attenborough, bakers in London are celebrating the legendary broadcaster's centenary with spectacular creations inspired by nature.

item.title: Black Friday: Where in Europe are shoppers the gloomiest?
item.description: As Black Friday deals hit Europe, new European Commission data show consumer confidence ranging from cautious optimism in Malta and near-neutral sentiment in Spain to deep gloom in Greece, while Italians cut back sharply on plans for big purchases.

item.title: Trump tariffs brought EU and Indonesia closer on trade, minister tells Euronews
item.description: US tariffs brought the EU and Indonesia closer, Indonesia's Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto said in an exclusive interview with Euronews. After a decade of talks, the two sides signed a deal last week, and the minister expects it to lift trade by 50% in three years.

item.title: 'Colourful and complicated': New London Museum promises to show city in all its glory
item.description: After a decade-long transformation costing more than €500 million, London Museum reopens its doors this weekend at the former Victorian General Market at Smithfield and it's billing itself as the world's largest city museum.

item.title: A green valley with a circular twist: Austria´s shapes the sustainable tech of tomorrow
item.description: Austria´s Green Tech Valley Cluster hosts 300 companies — including 20 global tech leaders — shaping the innovative and circular technologies of the future. They are developing solutions in sectors like hydropower, solar thermal, wind, recycling, batteries or electro-mobility — all made in Europe.

item.title: Watch: Police officer chases wild turkey on New Jersey highway
item.description: A wild turkey caused an unusual scene on the Garden State Parkway in New Jersey, prompting a police officer to chase the bird along the highway.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan reopen key border crossing for up to 100,000 travellers a day
item.description: The reopening comes as the EU seeks stronger transport and trade links with Central Asia. The upgraded checkpoint could also ease pressure on regional freight routes and support cross-border tourism.

item.title: EU budget summit collapses as row over money exposes clash over Europe's strategic tasks
item.description: The EU summit on the Union's common budget for 2028-2034 has initially failed. Some want to protect established spending, others to cut costs and mainly finance new strategic tasks, warns foreign policy expert Alexander Wolf of the Hanns Seidel Foundation in Berlin.

item.title: ‘Live and ongoing’ cyber incident takes down UK Department for Work and Pensions online services
item.description: The UK government department took the decision to take down the services as a precaution after it detected a cyber incident affecting its systems.

item.title: Meet Eba, the 11-year-old poop-sniffing dog helping to protect endangered orcas
item.description: Unlike most pooches, Eba spends her days on a boat - assisting scientists in the fight to save dwindling killer whale populations.
